original.target_description: Table 5 Model 5 openness contains both initial-level and mean-level-change unemployment terms; supplied description does not specify which estimand or whether a gender interaction is intended.

notes: Identity assessment: supplied source opens with Personality Change Following Unemployment and Christopher J. Boyce, Alex M. Wood, Michael Daly, and Constantine Sedikides. It identifies itself as a paper accepted for publication in the Journal of Applied Psychology, not the copy of record. This is a primary accepted manuscript matching the reference title, authors, topic, and longitudinal German study. The DOI is not printed in the supplied text, so DOI identity cannot be independently confirmed from this file alone. Source URL names a Stirling repository PDF. Full manuscript text includes methods, results, references and Table 5. No PDF path was supplied; no acquisition or rendering performed. Table 5 appears on manuscript pp. 53–54 rather than locator p.12. The broad relationship-between-unemployment-and-openness description and Table 5 locator do not distinguish intercept/initial level from slope/change or gender interaction. Candidate Model 5 dummy coefficients: intercept b=.708, SE=.477, beta=.150 (no significance star); slope b=-1.098, SE=.440, beta=-.318* (p < .05); female-by-unemployment slope b=1.586, SE=.689, beta=.306* (p < .05). The intercept female interaction is b=-1.545, SE=.747, beta=-.218* (p < .05). No candidate selected. Duration terms are also present but not named by this description. Candidate coefficients use the source-defined b personality SD = 1 metric. Target match stays null and statistic fields null; candidate evidence is retained here and in dispositions. Unassigned fields remain placeholders.
